India has made its new resident diplomatic mission in San José, Costa Rica, operational to broaden its diplomatic presence in central america and deepen bilateral engagement.Relations between India and Costa Rica have been gaining momentum, with both countries seeking to expand cooperation in trade, investment, pharmaceuticals and information technology.According to the ministry of external affairs (MEA), the Indian mission became operational on October 10.The ministry said the move would strengthen India's diplomatic outreach in central america and further consolidate ties with Costa Rica.The establishment of the resident mission is expected to facilitate closer political engagement between the two countries while promoting bilateral trade, investment and economic cooperation. Article Title: Rahul Gandhi, INDIA bloc's plea against EC still not listed yet as 14 defects remain
Article Text:
The registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition

NEW DELHI: The petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 other opposition leaders against the Election Commission of India (ECI) was not listed for hearing in the Supreme Court on Tuesday as defects flagged by the registry remain to be rectified, news agency PTI reported.According to the Supreme Court website, the registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition, including the absence of a clear copy of the identity card of Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, who is among the petitioners. The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the documents submitted.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut, who is also a petitioner, acknowledged the discrepancies on Tuesday and said the opposition would rectify them. Speaking to ANI, Raut said the petition had a shortfall of Rs 220 in the filing fee and referred to errors involving 14 documents.“There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair,” Raut said, adding that the leaders who participated in Monday's protest were petitioners in the legal challenge.The INDIA bloc leaders approached the Supreme Court following their march against the ECI on October 12, demanding accountability from the poll body over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Raut said the opposition wanted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and sought the restoration of names allegedly deleted from electoral rolls. He also accused the government of exerting political pressure on the ECI.On the opposition's next course of action, Raut said Rahul Gandhi had invited the leaders for tea on Tuesday evening, after which they would decide their future direction. He added that the leaders would remain in Delhi until the next steps were finalised.
Article Summary: The registry had pointed out 14 defects in the petition. The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the documents submitted. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut, who is also a petitioner, acknowledged the discrepancies on Tuesday and said the opposition would rectify them.

Article Title: Amit Shah reaffirms India's 'zero tolerance' policy against terror
Article Text:

What is BIMSTEC?

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called for stronger regional cooperation among BIMSTEC countries to combat terrorism , disrupt terrorist financing and organised crime, and prevent terrorist networks from finding safe havens in the region.Addressing the first Home Ministers’ Meeting of BIMSTEC countries in Delhi, Shah said India follows a policy of “zero tolerance” towards terrorism and stressed the need for collective action to strengthen regional security.“Hosting the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting is a matter of great pride and fortune for India. BIMSTEC, in a way, has become an essential platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. With the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India is going ahead today," Shah said.We have always been committed to peace, coexistence and human welfare. We continue to be committed to these even today. India has never believed in attacking any country or establishing dominance over them. India has always believed in upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every country and peaceful resolution of differences,” he added.Shah said the trust among BIMSTEC members was strengthened by the belief that the security arrangements of each country should contribute to the security of the others.He called for a collective resolve to ensure that terrorist networks could not find shelter, establish bases or training facilities, mobilise resources or carry out activities against other member countries.“India has always adopted a 'zero tolerance' policy against terrorism. The trust in our cooperation is strengthened by the sense that the security mechanism of every member country becomes helpful in the security of other member countries. Our mutual resolution should be to ensure that there is no scope or space for harbouring, recruiting, training, procuring resources, or carrying out activities against neighbouring nations in any part of the region,” he said.The home minister also urged member countries to cooperate on mutual legal assistance and extradition in accordance with their national laws and applicable agreements. He said such cooperation would strengthen efforts to bring criminals to justice.Highlighting counterterrorism and law enforcement as key areas of regional cooperation, Shah called for the exchange of actionable intelligence through existing nodal agencies and closer coordination to tackle terrorist financing and organised crime.He said the timely exchange of verified and actionable information on terrorists, their associates, criminal networks, financial channels and cross-border activities could strengthen collective security.Shah said efforts to curb narcotics smuggling would not succeed through the actions of individual countries alone, calling for a coordinated regional approach.“We must adopt a whole-of-region approach. The illegal proceeds from drugs provide financial strength to organised crime and are also used for terrorist financing. The diversion of precursor chemicals and transactions through the dark web make this challenge even more complex,” he said.The minister stressed that cooperation was necessary to tackle the links between drug trafficking, organised crime and terrorist financing.The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) is a regional grouping comprising seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.The grouping aims to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal and in its neighbourhood.
Article Summary: The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) is a regional grouping comprising seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. BIMSTEC has become an essential platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. The home minister also urged member countries to cooperate on mutual legal assistance and extradition.

Article Title: 'Congress will push him out as CM': Kumaraswamy after DKS being 'pushed' at Delhi march
Article Text:
Kumaraswamy said recent political developments in Karnataka were creating an “extremely bad political culture”.

NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Tuesday attacked the Congress party and Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar over an incident during the INDIA bloc's protest march in Delhi, warning that soon he "will be pushed out from CM post."Speaking to the media, Kumaraswamy said he was raising the issue with pain and would not comment further on Monday’s incident, in which Shivakumar was allegedly pulled back by security personnel during the march. However, he suggested that the episode could have wider political implications.“It is just the beginning, Congress will eventually push him out from CM post,” Kumaraswamy said, adding that “the day is not far when even his chair will be pulled away.”The remarks came after the BJP shared a video circulating online that appeared to show Congress leader Rahul Gandhi pulling Shivakumar by the collar as the two marched towards the Supreme Court to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Moments later, Shivakumar appeared to be pulled back as the Congress MP moves forward with the crowd.Kumaraswamy also said that said recent political developments in Karnataka were creating an “extremely bad political culture” that needed to end.He said the state was grappling with several pressing issues, including farmers’ demand for a scientifically determined price for sugarcane, drought conditions, and matters concerning the Bidadi township and the NICE project.However, he alleged that the controversy surrounding a sting operation had overshadowed these concerns after the chief minister raised the issue at a Cabinet meeting.Kumaraswamy also questioned Shivakumar’s alleged appointment of four retired police officers at his Sadashivanagar residence, claiming they had been tasked with gathering information about discussions among ministers.“Earlier, he had appointed only journalists to gather information for his office. Now, he has appointed four police officers to gather information about what is being discussed by ministers in his Cabinet. This discussion has begun within the police department,” Kumaraswamy claimed.On the sting operation case, he said the Nija Horata Samiti had filed a complaint in court and that an investigation was underway. He also alleged that a former chief minister had obtained a stay from the court in the matter.Kumaraswamy accused Shivakumar of initiating the sting operation controversy and said he should now face its consequences.“Mr Shivakumar, you were the one who initiated the sting operation. You nurtured it and allowed it to grow into a major controversy. Now you must face the consequences,” he said.Kumaraswamy also referred to the Prajwal Revanna case, alleging that videos were circulated on pen drives in Mandya and Hassan just four days before polling during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.He claimed that a recorded conversation and an audio clip involving a lawyer and others pointed to an alleged conspiracy to tarnish the Deve Gowda family. He also alleged that Shivakumar had spoken about getting complaints filed through women and the circulation of videos.Kumaraswamy further referred to the Ramesh Jarkiholi case, alleging that a conspiracy had been hatched against him. These claims were not independently established in the information provided.He urged Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah to speak out on the controversy and call for an inquiry. Referring to Siddaramaiah as his political teacher and a leader who had fought for the AHINDA community, Kumaraswamy said the chief minister should help establish the truth.“I don't say he should destabilise the government, but it is his teacher who fought for the AHINDA community from the political beginning. He should speak about these issues and bring out what is the truth and a CBI enquiry must be done,” he said.Kumaraswamy stressed that the controversy could damage the state’s reputation beyond the individuals involved.“It is not about one person or one family. These things will destroy the family culture in Karnataka and these kind of sting operations can bring very bad name to the whole state,” he said.“That is why I am demanding an enquiry that has to be done on the proposal of Chief Minister DK Shivakumar in Karnataka. I am also meeting Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the upcoming days to request the same,” he added.Kumaraswamy argued that approaching the court did not resolve the underlying issues and called for an inquiry into the alleged sting operations.He also criticised the Special Investigation Team (SIT) that investigated the Prajwal Revanna case, questioning its role and accusing it of remaining silent to protect certain people.“I’m asking, where is that SIT team, which did all these blenders in Karnataka and now keeping quite to safeguard some people with Distrupting agenda,” he said.Kumaraswamy added that he had not raised these issues when HD Revanna and his family were targeted and Prajwal Revanna was jailed following the SIT investigation.
Article Summary: HD Kumaraswamy attacked the Congress party and Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar over an incident during the INDIA bloc's protest march in Delhi. He said he was raising the issue with pain and would not comment further on Monday’s incident. The remarks came after the BJP shared a video circulating online that appeared to show Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.

Article Title: Last-minute question papers, more exam centres: Nandan Nilekani's plan to prevent NEET paper leaks
Article Text:
Nandan Nilekani proposes AI-generated question papers and wider computer-based testing to tackle exam paper leaks

NEW DELHI: Exam reforms task force head Nandan Nilekani on Tuesday suggested generating question papers at the last minute from a large question bank to reduce the risk of exam paper leaks. He also called for expanding computer-based testing across the country."Question papers create an economic incentive for them to be sold. So, the way to solve this is to really have a massive bank of questions, and only at the last minute generate the question paper for that day, and therefore the question of 'a' question paper goes away, and there's no economic incentive for that. That's one way to think about how to solve this," he said speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum.Asked whether artificial intelligence (AI) could generate exam papers on the day of a test, Nilekani replied, "Yeah. Sure. Yeah," as quoted by news agency ANI.Nilekani also stressed the need to move towards computer-based testing (CBT) for all examinations. He said India already had 150,000 locations where students could take tests, but the network needed to be expanded."The other thing is, of course, how to make sure all exams are done on a computer-based testing, and that requires a network of locations. We have 150,000 locations where a young boy or girl can take a test.That needs to be expanded," he said.Nilekani, who is heading a committee examining systemic reforms in examinations, said the panel would address these issues and indicated that the government was keen to implement its recommendations."I think these are all systemic issues which we will address in our committee. And the prime minister is very keen to implement our decisions," he said.The proposals come amid concerns over examination integrity following paper leak allegations, including those surrounding the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test ( NEET ).
Article Summary: Exam reforms task force head Nandan Nilekani suggests generating question papers at the last minute from a large question bank. He also called for expanding computer-based testing across the country. The proposals come amid concerns over examination integrity following paper leak allegations.

Article Title: Saudi-Houthi crisis: IndiGo cancels flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah
Article Text:
IndiGo, Akasa Air extend Saudi flight suspensions until October 17 amid security concerns

IndiGo and Akasa Air have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia until October 17, 2026, citing the evolving security situation in the Middle East.IndiGo said flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah would remain cancelled until October 17. In a travel advisory, the airline said it was sharing timely updates through the contact details provided at the time of booking. It added that its support teams were available to assist passengers."Your safety and well-being remain our top priority. We are in constant coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure safe operations," IndiGo said.Akasa Air also extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 17, citing the escalating security situation in the Middle East and the associated risks to safe flight operations.In its October 13 advisory, the airline said affected passengers could opt for a full refund, which would be credited to the original source of payment within seven days, or reschedule their travel at no additional cost. Passengers who booked through travel partners were advised to contact them directly for assistance."The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain our highest priority," Akasa Air said.This comes as one person was killed and 11 others injured in a fresh attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday.On Saturday, a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, triggering a fire.Saudi air defences also intercepted a cruise missile near the airport, destroyed a drone in the Eastern Province and intercepted a ballistic missile fired towards Khamis Mushait.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority confirmed a strike on Dammam airport late Sunday, adding that damage assessments and safety inspections were under way.The escalation has raised concerns over regional aviation, global oil supplies and shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime route linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis and planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
Article Summary: IndiGo, Akasa Air extend Saudi flight suspensions until October 17 amid security concerns. Comes as one person was killed and 11 others injured in a fresh attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday. Article Title: 'Serious setback': Ex-Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah on HC's move to strike down 56% quota
Article Text:
Siddaramaiah calls Karnataka HC’s 56% quota ruling a “serious setback”; Parameshwara hints at SC appeal.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah on Monday termed the Karnataka high court’s decision to strike down the law enhancing reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) a “serious setback” to historically marginalised communities.The law raised SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7%, taking the combined quota beyond the 50% ceiling."We respect the judiciary. However, the judgment raises fundamental questions about the BJP's handling of social justice. The BJP government increased SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7% ahead of the 2023 assembly elections, despite knowing that total reservation would exceed the 50% ceiling," news agency ANI quoted Siddaramaiah as saying."Why did the BJP announce enhanced reservation without first ensuring its constitutional sustainability? Was electoral advantage prioritised over lasting social justice?" he added.He said the demand followed “decades of struggle” and criticised the Centre for deferring Karnataka’s request to include the enhanced quotas in the Constitution’s Ninth Schedule.“Reservation is not charity,” Siddaramaiah said, calling for a review of the 50% ceiling and urging the state government to pursue legal remedies.Deputy chief minister G Parameshwara also described the ruling as a “serious development with far-reaching implications” for education and public employment.He questioned the previous BJP government’s decision to enact the law in October 2022 and criticised the Centre for delaying a decision on the Ninth Schedule proposal.Parameshwara said the state government “will examine all available legal remedies, including an appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court”. He added that Dalit and Adivasi children must inherit “greater opportunities, not prolonged legal uncertainty”.
Article Summary: Siddaramaiah calls Karnataka HC’s 56% quota ruling a “serious setback”; Parameshwara hints at SC appeal. Law raised SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7%.

Article Title: Missing pages, Rs 200 fee shortfall: SC flags 14 defects in INDIA bloc plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court registry Monday flagged 14 defects in a petition filed by the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.The registry asked the lawyer who filed the petition to submit a clear copy of the identity card of Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge , one of the co-petitioners, news agency PTI reported.The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the petition. It further pointed out a shortfall of Rs 220 in the court fee.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition, saying the INDIA bloc remained determined to hold the constitutional body accountable.Speaking to news agency ANI about the technical discrepancies in the petition, Raut said, "The petition that has been filed mentions that the fee is short by Rs 220, there are several errors, and there are facts about 14 documents mentioned in it. Well, it is possible. We have individual petitions in the names of Rahul Ji, Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, and all other India Bloc leaders. There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair.Confirming his participation in the legal challenge, Raut said, "Definitely, I am a petitioner. All the parties that were involved in yesterday's protest are all petitioners."On Monday, Rahul and several other opposition leaders marched to the Supreme Court to file the petition.The INDIA bloc leaders, led by Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, sought scrutiny of the Election Commission 's functioning, measures to prevent CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", alleged "arbitrary" voter deletions during SIR, and the system governing the use and deployment of electronic voting machines (EVMs).The petitioners included Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer.The opposition leaders sought a suspension of SIR without challenging its legality. They also called for eligible voters to be included in the electoral rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.After the CJI declined to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward."The petition also sought the formation of an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge and assisted by technical experts and other eminent citizens. The panel would be tasked with conducting an independent audit, within a fixed timeframe, of deletions and changes made to electoral rolls during SIR.The plea further requested the court to set up a panel to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".
Article Summary: SC flags over 10 defects in Rahul's plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition. Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward"

Article Title: Jennifer Garner bought back her family’s 55-acre Oklahoma farm in 2017; the land, held by her family since 1936, now inspires her organic children’s food business
Article Text:
PC: Forbes

Garner’s family farm has been in Oklahoma since 1936

How Garner joined the company behind organic children’s food

The family farm behind Garner’s farm-to-food philosophy

Once Upon a Farm expands its reach while focusing on nutrition access

Jennifer Garner’s work with organic children’s food has a connection to a place that has been part of her family’s life for generations.In Locust Grove, Oklahoma, a family farm that has been in Garner’s family since 1936 has helped shape her understanding of where food comes from and how children might develop a closer relationship with farming. Garner, who joined Once Upon a Farm as a co-founder in 2017, has spoken about the importance of making nutritious food more accessible to families. The business began with a practical problem: its original founders struggled to find the kind of organic baby food they wanted in local shops. Years later, the company has expanded across the United States, while Garner’s family farm remains a source of inspiration for its products.The Oklahoma property has been in Garner’s family located in Locust Grove; it has remained more than a backdrop to the actress’s childhood memories. Her uncle Robert still lives there and manages the farm, preserving a connection between the land and the family’s everyday life.Garner has described, "Once I started working for Once Upon a Farm, I loved the idea of connecting kids to the farm early on. And so here we are, connecting kids to the farm and it gets to be my family’s farm that’s been with us since 1936.One thing that I love about the farm is that my Uncle Robert still lives here. He is the holder of the stories and runs the farm to this day."Once Upon a Farm has developed into a national brand, the family’s agricultural roots offer a more personal reference point for its emphasis on organic ingredients and childhood nutrition.Once Upon a Farm was founded in 2015 by Cassandra Curtis and Ari Raz. Curtis wanted better options for her daughter after finding that the baby food available in nearby supermarkets did not meet her expectations. She began developing recipes herself, eventually bringing cold-pressure-protected baby food to retail shelves.Garner became involved in 2017, alongside John Foraker, the former chief executive of organic food company Annie’s. Foraker brought experience in building and scaling a consumer food business, while Garner offered the perspective of a parent who had encountered similar questions about what to feed young children.The company’s range has since grown beyond its original baby food products. It now includes organic snacks, smoothies and meals for children at different stages, with products distributed through major retailers across the country. Once Upon a Farm has described its aim as making nutritious food easier for families to find and serve.For Garner, the connection between agriculture and childhood nutrition has been a recurring theme in her work with the company. Her family’s Oklahoma farm provides a tangible example of where food begins, rather than presenting it solely as a finished product on a supermarket shelf.In material published by Once Upon a Farm, Garner spoke about wanting children to develop an early connection with farming. The fact that her own family’s property has remained in use for decades gives that idea a personal dimension. Her uncle’s continued involvement also means that farming knowledge has not been separated from the place where it was acquired.Once Upon a Farm has built its range around organic produce and refrigerated products, distinguishing its approach from the shelf-stable baby food that has long occupied a large part of the market.Once Upon a Farm’s expansion has taken it well beyond its original retail footprint. By August 2026, Forbes reported that the company was selling more than 40 products in over 25,000 stores. Its portfolio had grown to include drinkable smoothies and oat bars, alongside food for babies and young children.As reported by Forbes, the company also entered the public markets in February 2026, with an initial public offering valued at approximately $724 million. Garner marked the occasion at the New York Stock Exchange, but told Forbes that she preferred to concentrate on the company’s operations rather than follow daily movements in its share price.She holds a reported 7% stake in the business and serves as chief brand officer. Her responsibilities have included working with retailers and helping communicate the company’s purpose to families. Forbes estimated her stake to be worth about $55 million in its August 2026 report, although the value of publicly traded shares can change.Access to nutritious food has also become part of the company’s work. Garner told Forbes that obtaining certification for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, commonly known as WIC, was a major priority. The programme helps eligible low-income families buy approved foods, and Once Upon a Farm had secured certification in more than 20 states by the time of the report.
Article Summary: Jennifer Garner joined Once Upon a Farm as a co-founder in 2017. The company was founded in 2015 by Cassandra Curtis and Ari Raz. It sells organic snacks, smoothies and meals for children at different stages. Garner’s family farm in Oklahoma has been in her family since 1936.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Monday gave Delhi Police 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged electoral roll revision irregularities, offering the force the choice to decide when it could be held.However, just as the green light was sought, police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, throwing CJP's plan into uncertainty and prompting it to slam the move.Hours before party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka came to Parliament Street police station to submit a letter regarding its demand, barricades and security personnel had taken over adjacent roads.Even Firoz Shah Road, around 10 minutes away, had barricades and police personnel stationed along it.Closer to Parliament Street, access was restricted, with loudspeakers repeatedly warning: "Section 163 of BNSS is in place. Article Title: Same cause, separate protests: Why Congress and CJP are keeping their distance
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: "All the protests are one protest," Rahul Gandhi said when asked about the parallel demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Yet, despite their common demands, the Congress leader and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leadership have not shared a stage.Congress and other INDIA bloc leaders on Monday marched towards the Supreme Court over alleged electoral irregularities, while CJP continued its own campaign against the Election Commission.The two groups had also followed separate courses during the October 10 protests. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal and Left leaders were among those detained by Delhi Police. Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, was in Chennai, though he condemned the police action.Rahul Gandhi made "vote chori" a central political slogan of the opposition. CJP has also adopted it in its street demonstrations. But despite their overlapping demands, the two sides have largely pursued separate protest programmes.This has raised a political question: Why is Congress maintaining a distance from a movement that shares one of its biggest political demands?CJP's agitation against the Election Commission fits into a larger political battle that Congress has already made central to its opposition strategy.Rahul Gandhi's "vote chori" campaign has targeted alleged electoral irregularities in Karnataka, Haryana, Maharashtra and Bihar.The slogan "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod", frequently heard at CJP protests, also draws on the political language popularised by Rahul Gandhi.Former Congress national spokesperson Sanjay Jha, however, rejects the suggestion that the two sides are competing for political space."I don't think the battle is between the CJP and the Congress. All members of civil society, students, political parties, intellectuals, authors, activists, NGOs, everyone who's concerned about Indian democracy, are fighting both independently and collectively," he said.Describing CJP as a successful student movement, Jha credited it with bringing the issue to the forefront after investigations by The Indian Express."To say that there is any competition between the two is BJP propaganda, and we should not fall for that," he said.His argument is that the two groups can pursue the same demands without necessarily working together.However, their separate mobilisation has also brought attention to differences in their political approach and relationships with other opposition parties.The BJP and Election Commission, meanwhile, have rejected allegations of electoral manipulation, with the poll body maintaining that revisions are intended to identify ineligible entries and ensure the accuracy of electoral rolls.ALSO READ: 'Can't beat us, threaten us': Rahul thanks protesters after INDIA bloc march to SC The relationship between Congress and CJP is not simply one of competing claims. Their responses to the NEET-UG controversy in 2026 showed that they could support the same cause while maintaining separate political programmes.CJP emerged as a youth-led citizens' movement amid the controversy over alleged examination irregularities. It demanded accountability, education-system reforms and the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.On July 20, CJP organised a "Chalo Sansad" march from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament. Delhi Police stopped the march, citing violations of prohibitory orders and violence, while CJP alleged that police used excessive force against peaceful demonstrators.The following day, Congress organised a separate protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, led by Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.The party demanded Pradhan's resignation, a parliamentary discussion on paper leaks and education reforms, and an apology to students over the police action.Congress had been raising concerns over examination irregularities before CJP's march. Rahul Gandhi had met students in Kota and Dehradun, while he and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra visited injured students at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after the police action.The two sides supported similar demands but organised their programmes independently.That pattern is now visible again in the demonstrations against Gyanesh Kumar.The differences became more visible after CJP's recent outreach in Assam.Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh alleged that CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka had refused a courtesy meeting with Congress leaders, including Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi, despite Congress workers helping secure the release of detained CJP members.Singh claimed Ranka had declined to engage because the outreach was considered an AAP initiative."Aam Aadmi Party is known for piggy riding and hijacking issues of others," Singh alleged, accusing AAP of attempting to associate itself with movements led by others.These are Congress's allegations, and do not independently establish why CJP representatives declined the meeting.CJP co-convenor Saurav Das had also criticised what he described as a "self-declared liberal" ecosystem that believed "saving India" and the "Constitution" was its exclusive responsibility.The reference was politically significant because "Save the Constitution" has been a prominent part of Rahul Gandhi's campaign.Ranka also accused sections of that ecosystem of targeting CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke as the movement gained traction.Neither named Congress directly in the posts cited, but the subsequent exchange with Singh brought differences between the two sides into focus.Singh, however, argued that CJP should not be treated as any party's property."Let us keep it civil and issue centric. The cause is bigger than a political party," he said.The exchange suggested disagreements over political associations and coordination, even as both sides continued to raise similar demands.ALSO READ: 'Disclose EC files, set up audit panel': Key points from INDIA bloc's plea in SC The October 10 protest made the difference in political positioning more visible. Mamata Banerjee publicly backed CJP before the demonstration, saying, “We are fully supporting the Cockroach (Janta) Party and all the young generation and students. And my humble request, please stop these atrocities.”She later joined the protest in Delhi, pasting a band-aid over her mouth before being detained alongside TMC leaders. Kejriwal announced that he would attend with his family, while senior Left leaders backed the agitation and challenged restrictions imposed ahead of the demonstration.Congress had not announced participation in the same manner. But Rahul Gandhi's absence from Jantar Mantar did not mean silence on the police action. He condemned the mass detentions, accusing Delhi Police of “thuggery” and alleging that the government was encouraging violence against women and young protesters. He also announced plans for Congress and INDIA bloc leaders to meet the Chief Justice of India.Congress, therefore, continued to challenge the government while pursuing its own political mobilisation and institutional interventions. The distinction is between supporting a cause and joining a particular protest platform.CJP legal head Ratna Singh said the invitation remained open to all parties.“If the Congress is willing to come forward and join the protests, it is most welcome. Not just the Congress, but other parties too. Everyone should come together,” she said.“This is not the time to look at different groups protesting separately. We must see this as a unit, as a team effort, with people raising their voices against the wrongs happening in this country,” she added.Her appeal raises a question that extends beyond Congress: What does solidarity mean when parties agree on an issue but differ over how a protest should be organised, represented and politically sustained?The tensions around CJP have echoes of the 2011 India Against Corruption movement. The BJP publicly backed Anna Hazare's anti-corruption agitation against the Congress-led UPA government. Congress later accused the BJP and RSS of exploiting the movement to undermine its government.The movement's political afterlife was significant. Arvind Kejriwal, one of its prominent figures, went on to form the Aam Aadmi Party in 2012.The parallel is relevant to the present Congress-CJP friction. Congress spokesperson Reetam Singh has alleged that CJP's Assam outreach was viewed as an AAP initiative, accusing the party of “piggy riding and hijacking issues of others”.The allegation raises a question about whether Congress sees CJP not simply as a citizens' movement, but as a platform whose political associations and future trajectory matter.
Article Summary: CJP emerged as a youth-led citizens' movement amid the controversy over alleged examination irregularities. It demanded, education-system reforms and the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Despite their common demands, the Congress leader and the Cockroach Janta Party leadership have not shared a stage.

NEW DELHI: India has called for terrorist acts that meet the requisite threshold to be recognised within the framework of crimes against humanity at the United Nations.It also stressed that states must take the lead in preventing, investigating and prosecuting such crimes through their national legal and judicial systems.R Mythili, counsellor (legal adviser) at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, made the statement at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly's sixth committee during discussions on a proposed convention on the prevention and punishment of crimes against humanity.India called for the primacy of national and territorial jurisdictions, with due respect for “State sovereignty and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs”.It also said a new convention must “complement, not duplicate, existing international legal mechanisms”, cautioning against simply transferring existing international legal regimes into the proposed framework.India further called for “broadly accepted principles of international law, stronger national capacities, and transparent and inclusive negotiations” to strengthen the international framework for preventing and punishing crimes against humanity.

Essentials like transportation, education, clothing, shoes, and household goods are all getting more expensive,” he said.Ramesh argued that the burden of rising prices was being felt differently across income groups, with poorer households struggling to afford food and middle-class families facing pressure on their savings. Article Title: Peaceful protest fundamental to democracy, will review police action against protesters: Kharge

BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters who were detained on Monday, when police forcibly removed demonstrators and manhandled journalists covering the action.“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. It must be respected, protected and never suppressed,” Kharge said in a post on X. “I have issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted,” he added.Late on Monday, chief minister DK Shivakumar, had posted on X asking Bengaluru police commissioner to “look into this and ensure that the right to peaceful protest is protected”.Kharge also appealed to protesters to cooperate with the police and inform authorities in advance to ensure their safety and protect the rights of others. “The police are here to protect your rights, not to stand in the way of your voice,” he said.The announcement comes after dozens of protesters, including students, lawyers, activists, academics and senior citizens, were detained near KR Circle as they sought to march to the chief electoral officer’s office.They were demanding that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be scrapped and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign.The action also saw photojournalists covering the protest being assaulted and other journalists manhandled. Plainclothes personnel were among those seen acting aggressively towards protesters and journalists.An activist group, My Vote, My Right, said police confiscated placards and began detaining protesters before they could start the march. Its press release said people were pushed, dragged and forcibly taken away in buses. Police personnel were also seen beating young protesters and pulling at the clothes of women protesters, the group said.One photojournalist was beaten by four police personnel, while three other journalists were manhandled, according to the group.A photojournalist who witnessed the police action said an officer asked him to delete footage he had recorded of police assaulting students inside a bus. As journalists continued filming the detention of women protesters, police personnel objected.“One person came and said, delete it,” the photojournalist recounted. He said police personnel subsequently grabbed his phone, pushed him to the ground and threw the phone aside. Another officer pulled him by the collar, while personnel pushed him from behind and hit him on the leg. An officer also threatened to put him in jail.The incident had drawn criticism on social media, including from Arpita Das, associate professor of writing at Ashoka University, who said her daughter and a friend had been detained after joining the protest. She questioned why this was happening in a Congress-ruled state when young people were supporting the party’s position on SIR. Shivakumar’s X post was in response to Das’ post.The detentions in Bengaluru, incidentally happened on a day both Shivakumar and Kharge were protesting against SIR and police action against demonstrators in Delhi.On Monday, DCP (Central) Akshay M Hakay had said protesters had assembled near KR Circle without permission or prior intimation, contrary to high court directions that demonstrations be held at designated places. Police initially asked them to move to Freedom Park, but they did not comply and were taken into preventive custody before being released, he said.Hakay said police had acted with restraint and sensitivity. Acknowledging friction between police personnel and journalists, he described it as “completely unintentional” and said it had occurred in “straining circumstances”.Kharge Tuesday said: “Our responsibility is not merely to maintain law and order, but to create an environment where every citizen can express dissent freely, peacefully and without fear… In a democracy, peaceful dissent is not a threat to law and order. It is a right that law and order must protect,” he said.
Article Summary: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters. Article Title: 60% of 33 lakh who received SIR notices in Delhi are now verified
Article Text:
Disposal of SIR notices expedited after mid-September

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got SIR notices in Delhi have been verified after the Election Commission eased the verification process late last month.BLOs are now visiting homes to collect documents, instead of requiring people to appear for hearings at govt offices. Also, BLO have been empowered to make corrections for minor issues, such as spelling mistakes, without seeking extensive documentation.About 33 lakh voters, including chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and BJP veteran LK Advani got notices in Sept.While over 19 lakh voters were flagged for "logical discrepancies", including mismatches in names and age-related inconsistencies, nearly 14 lakh were classified as "unmapped" because their records could not be linked to the 2002 SIR. The notices sought clarification and supporting documents to verify eligibility for inclusion in the final SIR roll, scheduled for Dec 4.The office of the chief electoral officer of Delhi, in a post on X Monday, said: "We had started a proactive campaign to resolve these issues (discrepancies). By now around 20 lakh cases out of 33 lakh have been resolved. If any person has any grievance, please feel free to contact any of the 14,947 BLOs, 902 AEROs, 70 EROs, 13 DEOs or the CEO.No eligible voter will be excluded from the voter list."An official told TOI, "The disposal of SIR notices was very slow until the third week of Sept but picked up after we introduced new measures. Nearly 15,000 BLOs have been asked to clear at least 10 notices daily. In cases involving logical discrepancies, they have been instructed to verify the voter's age, Indian citizenship and ordinary residence in the constituency. Eligible voters will not be removed merely because of logical inconsistencies in their records. "A few BLOs told TOI they are using BLO declarations to verify voters with minor discrepancies, such as a missing letter in the name, after checking documents and getting the voter's signature on the declarations. Some BLOs said they had been using such declarations for quite some time now.AEROs, meanwhile, have been asked to upload details of resolved cases without delay. "We found that some AEROs were not uploading the cases they had already verified, partly because the deadline for completing the exercise was still weeks away. They have been instructed to ensure that resolved cases are uploaded promptly," said the official.In cases where voters could not be mapped to the previous electoral rolls, BLOs have been asked to clear the cases promptly after taking and checking prescribed documents, such as a voter's date of birth and other documents.Delhi's electoral roll listed 1.56 crore voters in January 2025, days before the assembly elections. In June, when the SIR began, this number had shrunk to 1.45 crore. The draft electoral roll published on Aug 31 had 97.5 lakh voters, with around 47.6 lakh names deleted.EC said a majority of these people had shifted homes and failed to submit enumeration forms. Those who have received SIR notices are among the 97.5 lakh voters. The disposal of SIR notices and completion of verification will continue until Nov 30.
Article Summary: Over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got SIR notices in Delhi have been verified. The Election Commission eased the verification process late last month. BLOs are now visiting homes to collect documents, instead of requiring people to appear for hearings at govt offices.

Article Title: Steelmaker to steer 440 crore revamp of 9 ITIs
Article Text: NEW DELHI : A Rs 440-crore overhaul will put ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) in charge of nine govt Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Gujarat and Andhra. The company will hold a 51% stake in entities managing the institutes under PM-SETU.Skill development ministry Monday signed shareholders' agreements covering five ITIs in Surat and four in Visakhapatnam. Rs 240 crore is earmarked for Surat and Rs 200 crore for Visakhapatnam. Centre and state govts will each hold 24.5% equity. SPVs will manage modernisation and operations. AM/NS India will implement the projects with New Age Makers' Institute of Technology as partner. Plans include modern workshops and laboratories, new trades, revised courses and more practical training.PM-SETU has Rs 60,000-crore outlay and aims to upgrade 1,000 govt ITIs and strengthen five National Skill Training Institutes. Funding includes Rs 30,000 crore from Centre, Rs 20,000 crore from states and Rs 10,000 crore from industry.
Article Summary: A Rs 440-crore overhaul will put ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India in charge of nine govt Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Gujarat and Andhra. The company will hold a 51% stake in entities managing the institutes under PM-SETU.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi venting electoral frustration through protests: BJP
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: It is not Election Commission (EC) but Congress's own "visionless" leadership that is behind its long run of poll defeats, BJP said Monday, stating that an "unstable, anarchist and unserious" Rahul Gandhi has turned to street protests to vent his frustration over popular rejection.Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan quizzed Congress over its losses even in recent bypolls and factional fights besetting its state units from Karnataka to Punjab and UP, asserting that the party had lost people's trust for long.BJP MP Anurag Thakur questioned INDIA bloc's decision to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant following its march Monday, saying it amounted to Rahul and his party threatening the judiciary over a sub-judice matter.Hitting out at Rahul, Anurag said it was unfortunate for the country that the leader of the opposition has total disregard for facts and rules, and can only spread anarchy, denigrate constitutional institutions and defame India globally. "Vote chori is on his lips, but what he is doing is belittling popular mandate," he said.BJP also flayed Rahul for projecting the protests as "Shivji ki barat", recalling the previous Congress govt's decision questioning the existence of Lord Ram.In fact, it involves a collection of hooligans determined to stoke disorder with support from foreign forces inimical to India, the party alleged.Asked about Rahul's claims like half of police personnel sympathising with Opposition's protests, Chouhan cited a Hindi proverb to allege that the Congress MP was worth lakhs of liars. "If the Opposition is levelling allegations, then it is also its job to offer proof. It should support an independent probe into its claims. Democracy does not give one the licence to denigrate public mandate," Anurag said, adding that, unlike Congress, BJP has a history of defending the Constitution, as in the Emergency.Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra said "Rahul Gandhi, who once tore up a bill introduced by his own govt, has disrespected the dignity of Supreme Court today, proving that he has become the most anarchic leader in the country.""By disrespecting the dignity of Supreme Court and the Chief Justice of India today, Rahul Gandhi has forfeited the moral right to file a petition before Supreme Court," he added. "His anarchic conduct today has established that if he dislikes any verdict of Supreme Court tomorrow, he will take to the streets against it as well".BJP ally Chirag Paswan, who has at times taken a position different from BJP's, also hit out at Rahul, saying SC has already given its judgment on SIR and asking if he was not pressuring the court with street protests.
Article Summary: BJP MP Anurag Thakur questioned INDIA bloc's decision to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. He said it amounted to Rahul and his party threatening the judiciary over a sub-judice matter. Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan quizzed Congress over its losses.

Article Title: SC to government: Cap prices of non-patented medicines
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said there was no rationale for controlling the price of a few scheduled medicines and allowing the rest to be sold at inflated prices as all medicines are essential. It suggested a uniform rule limiting the MRP to not more than 16% above the price to the retailer (PTR).

SC to government: There is a great divide... why can’t you control the entire range of drugs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the Centre failing to give even "one justification" to the satisfaction of the court in favour of patients for keeping the maximum retail price of medicines at exorbitant levels but also accepting that profit margins for drugs and medical consumables reach up to 1,000%, Supreme Court on Monday said that the price of all non-patented drugs and consumables should also be controlled and it should not be confined only to anti-cancer medicines as done by govt recently.As solicitor general Tushar Mehta and ASG Aishwarya Bhati informed SC about the decision to cap the trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of the maximum retail price, the court appreciated govt's decision but raised questions on why pricing of other medicines should not be capped. The bench pointed out various examples to drive home the point that patients are fleeced because of sky-high pricing.This relates to only cancer drugs. What about the overall? For an ordinary cardiac stent, Indian made stent, price to retailer (PTR) is Rs 5,000 but MRP is Rs 25,000... This is not even a tip of the iceberg. It (decision) has come only because of harsh observation from the court,” the bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked SG Tushar Mehta and also applauded his intervention resulting in a quick decision.It said the price of a drip line for saline for the retailer is Rs 11 but the MRP is around Rs 270. It said MRP for Azithromycin is Rs 78.29 but the PTS (price to stockist) is Rs 28.5.“There is a great divide... There are thousands of examples,” court said, asking govt to explain why all non-patented medicines shouldn’t be brought under price control.“Give me just one justification in favour of patients (for not controlling the prices). Why can’t you control the entire range of drugs?” the bench asked the ASG.Bhati submitted that areas with lower sales, such as rural areas, may require higher margins for the retailer so as to provide sufficient income and livelihood to the retailer, failing which the access to and availability of drugs in such areas may be adversely affected. She told the bench the Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world. “If there is too much intervention by govt, it will lead to the market suffering. It will affect availability.”But court said all the justifications given by govt were not in favour of patients who had to pay the higher price. Intervening in the proceedings, the SG submitted govt was not averse to the plea and the bench also made it clear that its proceeding was only intended to “strengthen the hands of the govt and nothing else”.Govt, in its affidavit, said, “Another area of concern in the sector is supply of consumables in hospitals, where margins of 100-1000% or more are prevalent, along with a tendency of hospitals to purchase consumables that have a high MRP, with a low price to the distributor/hospital.”It admitted that patients have a very low bargaining position vis-a-vis the hospital, and a patient’s knowledge of drugs, their substitutes and their prices is also limited.“These bargaining and information asymmetries result in malpractices despite strong competition among manufacturers, leading to the need for regulation. That hospitals purchase medicines from manufacturers who provide the highest trade margin and then sell those to patients at the MRP, with margins ranging from 170% to 700% or more in the case of anti-cancer (oncology) drugs,” the affidavit said.The apex court thereafter adjourned the case for Oct 27.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said there was no rationale for controlling the price of a few scheduled medicines. It suggested a uniform rule limiting the MRP to not more than 16% above the price to the retailer (PTR)SC to government: There is a great divide... why can’t you control the entire range of drugs?

Article Title: Jantar Mantar out as protest hub; 3 new venues named
Article Text:
Shifting protests to Burari will reduce chances of traffic congestion: Police

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For decades, Jantar Mantar offered protesters a place within earshot of Parliament and the seat of govt they sought to hold accountable. Now they will have to make themselves heard from further away.Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari ground in the north and CBD ground in Shahdara have been designated as the city's new protest sites, replacing Jantar Mantar Road. An order issued by police commissioner Anurag Kumar on Oct 11 said the decision followed recommendations by a ministry of home affairs committee set up to identify suitable venues where citizens could exercise their right to protest.The order said: "On the committee recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified".While the protest site is called Jantar Mantar, the protests never took place inside the 18th-century, ASI-protected astronomical observatory. They were held on the adjoining Jantar Mantar Road, the starting point of many historic movements.On the face of it, the road is hardly an ideal protest venue. Hemmed in by bungalows and shops, it offers limited space. But crowds find room, spilling into lanes and roads, as was seen during June-July CJP protests and the 2011 India Against Corruption movement.But its location more than makes up for the lack of space. Around 3km from Parliament and barely a kilometre from Connaught Place, it sits amid key govt buildings. It also offers the practical comforts a protest site needs: water, inexpensive food, toilets and tree shade. But its biggest advantage, however, may be that it comes free.The alternatives come with a price. Booking Ramlila Maidan for functions costs Rs 66,080, while Burari and CBD grounds cost approximately Rs 90,000 each (without security deposit). No separate booking category for protests has been introduced yet.Jantar Mantar’s denotification as a protest site came after Supreme Court, on Oct 9, asked authorities to designate a suitable alternative venue for protests. During the hearing, the CJI-led bench said, “The govt and parties are agreeable to the suggestion that it is high time to identify and designate a proper protest site, instead of Jantar Mantar, with basic amenities like water, toilets and healthcare facilities. The competent authorities would consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision in this regard.”An officer said at Jantar Mantar, a crowd beyond 1,000 leads to crowding and traffic congestion on approach roads. Another officer said the presence of sensitive installations in the vicinity was also a security concern.“If someone disguises themselves as a protester and then moves towards a sensitive installation, it could pose a security threat,” the officer said.Ramlila Maidan can accommodate a crowd of up to 50,000, while Burari ground, which is the largest of the three sites, can hold more than 50,000 people. CBD Ground in Shahdara is across 12 acres.A senior police officer said Ramlila Maidan can host protests and large gatherings. Organisers must apply 10-12 days in advance, after which police coordinate with them on turnout, venue requirements, timings, VIP attendance and the agenda. In 2011, the Anna Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which later gave rise to AAP, shifted from Jantar Mantar to Ramlila Maidan as crowds swelled.The proposed shift from Jantar Mantar also raises questions about managing exceptionally large gatherings. One of the organisers of Ramlila events claimed that the turnout at some programmes could exceed 50,000, potentially putting pressure on the arrangements at the designated venues.Police sources said the area of the site at Shahdara will be finalised before infrastructure is set up. With malls, banquet halls and other commercial facilities nearby, clearly demarcating the venue and managing traffic will be key, they said. Once the site is finalised, police infrastructure, including a police post, would be made, the sources added.Burari Ground is an open space. Police sources said the likelihood of such gatherings significantly affecting traffic was relatively low here.
Article Summary: Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari ground in the north and CBD ground in Shahdara have been designated as the city's new protest sites. Shifting protests to Burari will reduce chances of traffic congestion: Police.

Article Title: CJI: Don't drag SC into political battlefields or bring politics to court
Article Text:
CJI rejects INDIA bloc leaders’ request for meeting over ‘vote chori’

Wherever identified locations are there, protests can be held: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after CJI Surya Kant turned down Congress leadership's request to meet them privately on their "vote chori" charge, saying doing so will violate the principle of separation of powers, SC Monday reiterated that it should not be dragged into political battlefields nor politics be brought into the court."We are not concerned with political parties or their activities. But courts should not be dragged into such kinds of things," said a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.In an email response, through which he turned down the request from leaders of opposition in the two Houses of Parliament, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, for a face-to-face meeting, CJI had pointed out to them that it was duty-bound to hear petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and those challenging SIR, and indicated that the court will hear those on priority.The CJI-led bench Monday emphasised the need for it to exercise restraint and not enter the political thicket while hearing the complaint that protests and barricades were obstructing lawyers from working.At the commencement of proceedings, senior advocate Atmaram Nadkarni sought urgent hearing on a writ petition filed by a lawyer, saying he could not represent his client at an international arbitration because of protests and preventive measures.Nadkarni was joined by SCBA president Pradeep Rai who said the right to protest must co-exist with the right of other citizens to move and function without hindrance. SC agreed to list both the petitions for hearing on Tuesday along with pleas by Shailendra Mani Tripathi, opposition MPs M A Baby, Manoj Jha and Menaka Guruswamy, who have accused police of using excessive force to quell protests.Rai said, “Institution is performing its institutional duty and we are doing our professional duties. Political parties must not interfere with our domain.”CJI Surya Kant, while saying that court would not wade into others’ turf, said, “Democratic institutions should be allowed to function peacefully and there should not be any impediment in the functioning or movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants.”Following Nadkarni and Rai, advocate G Sankaranarayanan mentioned another petition repeating what was argued — detention of senior advocate Shadan Farasat in an “unseemly” manner — before SC on Sunday and suggested that asking protesters to exercise restraint, be peaceful and cooperate when police was using excessive force, was not fair.“I know SC has repeatedly said we must try to cooperate and exercise restraint. For once I would hope that court would say the same thing to police. That has not come from this bench so far. I am hoping that happens because of excesses they are allowing... the hooligans were roaming around with sticks,” he said.“They have hit children on the head and put out videos and proudly posted the videos saying they have done this and police have done nothing. And we are being told to exercise restraint. I do not know what we have done to be told to exercise restraint. At some point the bench will come to the rescue of the bar and the citizens of this country and send a strong message to the police,” he added.CJI agreed to list the petition on Tuesday but stressed yet again: “I will not allow SC or SC campus to become a political battlefield. We do not want advocates and lawyers to be part of the political battles inside the court premises. Wherever identified locations (for protest) are there, the protests can be held there.”
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant turned down the request from leaders of opposition in the two Houses of Parliament, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, for a face-to-face meeting. CJI pointed out to them that it was duty-bound to hear petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and those challenging SIR.

Article Title: INDIA bloc files petition in SC on SIR voter deletions
Article Text:
INDIA bloc seeks complete files, objections by ECs to SIR, access logs, meeting minutes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, undertook their march to Supreme Court on Monday to file a joint petition seeking intense scrutiny into a host of issues - functioning of EC, preventing CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", "arbitrary" deletion of voters during SIR, and the architecture governing use and deployment of EVMs.Rahul and other petitioners - Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer - sought suspension of SIR without questioning its legality, and, inclusion of eligible voters in rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.On CJI's refusal to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward." The petition requested the court to set up a panel led by a retired SC judge, comprising technical experts and persons of eminence to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".The petitioners also wanted the panel to ‘review processes, procedures, protocols and technical architecture governing EVMs’.They said, “The validity of SIR does not dispense with the requirement that each decision taken in its implementation must conform to Constitution, governing statutes and applicable rules.”The present plea is instituted in the larger public interest of safeguarding the constitutional right of every eligible citizen to vote, maintaining institutional independence and collective functioning of EC, and ensuring that the preparation and revision of poll rolls are carried out transparently, lawfully and in a manner that inspires public confidence in the democratic process, the opposition functionaries argued.Flagging alleged unlawful modification of Form 6, used for enrolment of new voters, the petitioners, through advocate Prasanna S, said, “Addition of an unauthorised condition to a statutory form may impose an unlawful burden upon eligible citizens seeking registration, particularly first-time voters, and may result in the exclusion of persons otherwise entitled to be enrolled.”The SC registry pointed out several defects in the petition, and the counsel said he will cure them in due course.The opposition members also objected to centralised and opaque functioning of ECINET and ERONET poll rolls database and the “large-scale exclusion of voters without adequate notice, hearing or an effective mechanism for restoration in case of wrongful or erroneous deletions”.Invoking fundamental rights of people under Articles 14, 19, 21 read with Article 324 (EC) of the Constitution, they sought a direction from SC to EC to produce in court “complete files, agendas, minutes, file noting and objections recorded by election commissioners in respect of each of the disputed decisions related to SIR, together with relevant ECINET and ERONET access logs and complete file recording on EC’s June 24, 2025 decision to commence SIR across the country”.Pending decision on the petition, they said EC must function as per the mandate of the Constitution in a democratic manner and ensure Form 6 conformed to Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.They wanted EC to “publish, booth-wise, the names of all electors deleted during the SIR, together with the reasons for each deletion and a breakdown of deletions by gender and age, and to provide an effective and functional mechanism for restoring the names of electors found eligible for inclusion in the poll rolls”.
Article Summary: Opposition INDIA bloc members, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, undertook their march to Supreme Court on Monday. They sought intense scrutiny into a host of issues - functioning of EC, preventing CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", "arbitrary" deletion of voters during SIR, and the architecture governing use and deployment of EVMs.

Article Title: Panel to address grievances of sugarcane growers
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Govt Monday announced establishment of a high-level committee within a week to address the grievances of sugarcane farmers over discrepancies in sugar recovery, weighment and payments. The announcement was made at a meeting chaired by agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan which was attended by farmers from Maharashtra and Karnataka.Chouhan and food minister Pralhad Joshi held detailed discussions with a delegation of farmers from the two major cane-growing states. About 80-90 farmers from different organisations attended, along with state ministers.The committee will comprise representatives of the Centre, Karnataka and Maharashtra govts, farmer organisations and sugar mills, besides subject-matter experts and scientists.With sugar mills set to begin crushing in the 2026-27 season, which started on Oct 1, farmers have sought a higher support price, citing rising production costs.They have also demanded that MSP of sugar be raised from Rs 31/kg to Rs 50/kg.The panel will examine technical aspects and submit its recommendations within a stipulated timeframe
Article Summary: The announcement was made at a meeting chaired by agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The committee will comprise representatives of the Centre, Karnataka and Maharashtra govts, farmer organisations and sugar mills. The panel will examine technical aspects and submit its recommendations within a stipulated timeframe.
